Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be compact and let $L_0,L_1\subset X$ be compact smooth submanifolds whose intersections are finite and transverse. Suppose fixed disjoint coordinate neighborhoods of the intersection points take both submanifolds to linear subspaces, as provided by the product generator charts. Then there is a smooth map
$$\mathcal E:\{(x,v)\in TX:|v|_g<\epsilon\}\longrightarrow X$$
for some $\epsilon>0$, with $\mathcal E(x,0)=x$, $d_v\mathcal E(x,0)=I$, and $\mathcal E(x,v)\in L_j$ whenever $x\in L_j$, $v\in T_xL_j$. The map $(x,v)\mapsto(x,\mathcal E(x,v))$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open neighborhood of the diagonal in $X\times X$ after shrinking its domain. Its inverse for sufficiently close pairs in $L_j\times L_j$ takes values in $TL_j$.

On smaller fixed generator neighborhoods it is exactly coordinate addition:
$$q(\mathcal E(x,v))=q(x)+dq_xv$$
for all sufficiently small $v$. Derivatives of every fixed order of this addition and its inverse are uniformly bounded on smaller neighborhoods in finite coordinate covers. This is a genuine finite-dimensional boundary-preserving local addition, not an assumption about a Sobolev map space.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

Let $k,n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^k$, with $Df(a)$ invertible. Then every local inverse supplied by the inverse function theorem at $a$ is $C^k$. In its inverse neighbourhood it satisfies

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}.$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: At a point of $L_e$ split $TX=TL_e\oplus J_bTL_e$. Define the real bundle map $A^e_a$ by $A^e_av=v$ and $A^e_a(J_bv)=J^e_av$ for $v\in TL_e$. On these two summands it satisfies $A^e_aJ_b=J^e_aA^e_a$, including $A^e_aJ_b(J_bv)=-v=J^e_aJ^e_av$. Its block matrix is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}I&C_a\\0&D_a\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Put $g(v,w)=\omega(v,J_bw)$ on $TL_e$. Since this subspace is Lagrangian, $$g(v,D_av)=\omega(v,J^e_av)>0\quad(v\ne0).$$ Thus $D_{a,r}=(1-r)I+rD_a$ is invertible for every $0\le r\le1$: a vector in its kernel would have $(1-r)|v|_g^2+r g(v,D_av)=0$. Consequently $A^e_{a,r}=I+r(A^e_a-I)$ is an explicit smooth invertible bundle path fixing $TL_e$ pointwise. It equals I wherever $J^e_a=J_b$. Tameness, not compatibility of $J^e_a$, is the property used here. [A1, given, construct, algebra]

Use $N_e=J_bTL_e$ as the smooth normal complement. The map $\Psi_e(p,n)=\mathcal E(p,n)$ on its disk bundle has differential $(v,n)\mapsto v+n$ on the zero section, hence is a local diffeomorphism by [F2]. Compactness gives one positive radius on which it is injective: otherwise collisions tending to the zero section have a convergent base subsequence, contradicting the local inverse there. Define the germ $$H^e_{a,r}(\Psi_e(p,n))=\mathcal E(p,A^e_{a,r}n).$$ A tangent component of $A^e_{a,r}n$ is allowed in the ambient local addition. This germ fixes $L_e$, has full derivative $A^e_{a,r}$ along it, and is identity for $r=0$. The parameter version of [F2] and compactness of the cube times $[0,1]\times L_e$ give common smaller domains and common image neighborhoods on which these are smooth invertible germs. Injectivity is proved by the same collision argument uniformly in the compact parameters. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]

On this common image neighborhood set $V^e_{a,r}=(\partial_r H^e_{a,r})\circ(H^e_{a,r})^{-1}$. It is smooth, zero along $L_e$, and identically zero near every generator where the bundle path was identity. Extend it by a smooth finite cutoff, equal to one on the compact union of the images of a still smaller closed tube, and zero off the common germ image neighborhood. Its support can be kept in the prescribed torus neighborhood and off the protected set. Compactly supported finite-chart flows in [F1] integrate it for $0\le r\le1$, with all parameters. Uniqueness identifies this global flow with $H^e_{a,r}$ on a still smaller tube: every such germ trajectory remains in the cutoff-one region by the chosen compact image inclusion. In particular the flow has the prescribed full derivative and fixes every point of $L_e$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, construct]

Make the two constructions compatible. Remove smaller generator neighborhoods whose closures lie in the larger neighborhoods where every $A^e_{a,r}=I$. The remaining compact pieces of $L_0$ and $L_1$ are disjoint and have positive separation. The nonzero germ velocities can therefore be cut off in neighborhoods avoiding the OTHER torus and the smaller generator neighborhoods. Each resulting global flow is identity on a neighborhood of the other torus; although it may act near its own torus, it fixes that torus pointwise. Compose the two flows to obtain $P_{a,r}$. Their supports may be chosen disjoint outside the fixed generator regions; in any case their derivatives along the other torus are identity, so $dP_a=A^e_a$ on $L_e$. Step1.1 gives $P_a^*J^e_a=J_b$ there. At $r=0$ both flows are identity. If both boundary structures equal $J_b$ on a parameter face, all corresponding germ velocities are zero, so the constructed flow is literally identity on that face. There is no assumed return-holonomy identity. [F1, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

Compact parameter domains, compact vector-field support and the explicit smooth Picard dependence give uniform bounds on each finite derivative of $P_{a,r}$ and its inverse; its inverse is the reverse compact flow. If $a=a(s)$ is stationary on source-end collars, so is $P_{a(s)}$. Put $u(s,t)=P_{a(s)}v(s,t)$, $K=P_{a(s)}^*J(s,t)$ and $W=-(dP_{a(s)})^{-1}\partial_sP_{a(s)}$. The chain rule gives $$u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v_s+K(s,t,v)v_t=W(s,v).$$ Because every $P_a$ fixes both tori POINTWISE, $\partial_sP_a=0$ there; hence $W|_{L_0\cup L_1}=0$. This does not imply neighborhood vanishing. The full values of K on the physical boundaries are precisely $J_b$, and W is independent of t. Stationary end diffeomorphisms conjugate the actual endpoint equations and linearizations by their bounded invertible differentials, including their integer Sobolev realizations. The natural taming form for K is $P_a^*\omega$, not a falsely unchanged $\omega$. [F1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

In the symmetric-product case lift each compact vector field away from the discriminant using the local inverse of the ordered quotient differential. Its finite-cover local definitions agree by uniqueness and are permutation-equivariant. The original vector field is identically zero near the discriminant; its lift is consequently zero on an open neighborhood of every partial diagonal and extends smoothly by zero there, with bounded derivatives on the compact product. It is also zero near the prescribed point divisors. Integrating this actual lifted field gives a smooth equivariant flow, and uniqueness of the quotient flow proves $q\widetilde P_{a,r}=P_{a,r}q$. Thus all prescribed divisors and collision strata are genuinely preserved. Every construction used finite choices and specified countable Picard limits. The asserted normalization, relative prescriptions, lift and exact equation follow. [F1, A1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct] ∎

boundaries.evidence: steps 2.1 through 4.1: empty intersection or no protected sets simply removes cutoffs; finite torus pieces remain separated.
steps 1.1 and 4.1: zero jet difference yields literal identity flow on prescribed parameter faces.
steps 1.1 through 3.1: one torus or one normal complex direction uses the same positive normal-block proof.
steps 1.1 and 4.1: boundary structures are only tame, not assumed compatible; convex normal blocks retain positive symmetric part.

steps 2.1 through 6.1: finite charts and explicit Picard iteration require no stronger choice.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold, and let $L_0,L_1$ be compact transverse submanifolds of half its dimension with finite intersection. On a neighborhood of their union supply a symplectic form $\omega$ making them Lagrangian, and a compatible almost-complex structure $J_b$. Supply common disjoint linear generator charts near their intersections. Let $a$ range over a compact finite-dimensional cube. For $e=0,1$ supply smooth $\omega$-tame complex structures $J^e_a$ along $L_e$, equal to $J_b$ on larger fixed generator neighborhoods. A prescribed protected closed subset of $X$ is disjoint from both tori and the generator neighborhoods.

There are smooth parameter-dependent diffeomorphisms $P_a:X\to X$, isotopic to the identity through an explicitly constructed smooth family $P_{a,r}$, $0\le r\le1$, fixing both $L_e$ POINTWISE, identity near the protected set and on smaller generator neighborhoods, such that
$$ (P_a^*J^e_a)|_{L_e}=J_b|_{L_e}. $$
Every prescribed parameter face on which both $J^e_a=J_b$ along $L_e$ has $P_{a,r}=\mathrm{Id}$ for all $r$. All finite derivatives have uniform bounds on compact parameter sets. No equality on an entire torus neighborhood is asserted.

When $X$ is a smooth symmetric product, the protected set contains a neighborhood of its discriminant and its prescribed point divisors, and all nonidentity support lies in the off-diagonal locus, the construction has a genuine smooth permutation-equivariant ordered lift, identity near the partial diagonals and prescribed point divisors. It does not use a symmetric power of a nonholomorphic surface map.

Let $\Sigma$ be a closed Riemann surface, $m\ge1$, and $p\in\Sigma$. In the complex symmetric product $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ let $E_p=\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$. Let $L_0,L_1\subset X$ be compact submanifolds disjoint from $E_p$. Suppose $J_t$ agrees with the fixed complex structure of $X$ on one neighborhood of $E_p$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. Let $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ be a smooth solution of $\partial_\tau u+J_t(u)\partial_tu=0$, with boundary on $L_0,L_1$ and uniform limits as $\tau\to\pm\infty$ at points of $L_0\cap L_1$.

The intersections of $u$ with $E_p$ are a finite collection of interior points, each with positive integral local intersection multiplicity. Their sum is nonnegative, and it is zero exactly when $u$ avoids $E_p$. In pointed Heegaard data, with $L_0,L_1$ the product tori and $p$ any marked point, this proves nonnegativity of the domain multiplicity $n_p(u)$ whenever it is defined by intersection with $E_p$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(\Sigma,j)$ be a closed Riemann surface with positive area form $\eta$, and put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$, $m\ge1$, with its induced complex structure $J_0$. Let $q:\Sigma^m\to X$ be the quotient, $\Delta\subset X$ its repeated-point locus, and $\Omega=\sum_{l=1}^m\operatorname{pr}_l^*\eta$. Off $\Delta$ the permutation-invariant form $\Omega$ descends to a smooth form $\omega$ on $X\setminus\Delta$. Equip $X$ with any smooth Riemannian metric $g$.

Let $L_\alpha,L_\beta$ be product tori formed from two finite systems of pairwise disjoint attaching curves, with transverse intersections between the systems. Suppose a smooth path $J_t$ agrees with $J_0$ on a neighborhood $V$ of $\Delta$ and tames $\omega$ on $X\setminus V$. Let $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ be a smooth $J_t$-holomorphic strip, with boundary on these tori, finite $g$-Dirichlet energy, and uniform limits at both ends to intersection generators. For each complementary region $R$ of the attaching curves write $n_R(u)$ for the signed intersection multiplicity of $u$ with $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ at a generic $p\in R$.

There is a constant $C$ depending only on the fixed geometric data and the path, independent of $u$, such that
$$E_g(u)=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R\times[0,1]}(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)\,dsdt\le C\sum_R n_R(u)\int_R\eta.$$
In particular energies of all such representatives with one fixed domain are uniformly bounded. The finite-energy hypothesis here is explicit; no assertion that arbitrary asymptotically convergent smooth solutions automatically have finite energy is included.

Assume Countable Choice. Give an actual complete singly pointed Heegaard diagram of ANY closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$, with transverse attaching systems, one-ball compression cuts, basepoint $z$, a reference orientation-compatible Riemann surface structure and a positive area form. Suppose it is GLOBALLY weakly admissible: every nonzero periodic region domain with $n_z=0$ has both signs. Broad smooth tangencies of auxiliary compression-disk witnesses are permitted.

There is a choice of surface complex structure, protected region and marked-divisor neighborhoods, common product-integrable generator charts and a nearly symmetric tame path constant on genuine endpoint time collars, for which EVERY nonconstant finite-energy strip with $n_z=0$ has onto actual fixed-end Cauchy--Riemann operator. There are finitely many actual index-one strip orbits with $n_z=0$, across all endpoints and Whitney classes, and their modulo-two count matrix satisfies $\widehat\partial^2=0$. These actual chosen counts therefore define a finite chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$.

Every complete pointed splitting can first be made globally weakly admissible by the finite basepoint-avoiding curve isotopies in [[thm-complete-pointed-heegaard-diagrams-admit-globally-weak-admissible-isotopies]]. Consequently a chosen-data complex of this kind can be obtained from every supplied complete splitting of general $Y$. This does not identify complexes before and after those isotopies. It neither imposes global admissibility on ALL inputs of the original sector-specific definition nor proves the construction for every merely sector-admissible diagram. Auxiliary-choice and Heegaard-move invariance, Spin-c decomposition, relative or absolute grading, plus/infinity and cobordism maps remain separate. In genus zero the empty generator gives the one-dimensional complex with zero differential; a possibly empty positive-genus generator set is not asserted to have nonzero homology.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, and let $J(s,t,x)$ be a smooth family of almost complex structures on $X$, defined for $(s,t)$ in an open subset $U\subset\mathbb R^2$. Suppose the norms of $J$ and its derivatives through total order two, using the Levi-Civita connection in $X$ and ordinary derivatives in $s,t$, are uniformly bounded. Then there are constants $a,b\ge0$, depending only on these bounds and $g$, such that every smooth solution
$$u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$$
has energy density $e=(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)/2$ satisfying
$$\Delta e\ge-ae^2-be.$$
Consequently there are $r_0,\varepsilon_0>0$ depending only on the same data such that, whenever $\overline B_r(z)\subset U$, $0<r\le r_0$, and $\int_{B_r(z)}e<\varepsilon_0$, one has
$$|du(z)|_g^2\le\frac{32}{3\pi r^2}\int_{B_r(z)}e.$$
These are interior estimates for smooth actual solutions. No boundary estimate or higher-derivative compactness is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary, with a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, and let $L\subset X$ be a compact embedded submanifold without boundary of half its real dimension. Let $J(s,t,x)$ be a smooth uniformly $C^2$ bounded family of almost complex structures for parameters in a neighborhood of a closed upper half-disk. Suppose $J(s,0,x)=J_b(x)$ for $x\in L$, independently of $s$, where $TL\cap J_bTL=0$.

There is a smooth Riemannian metric $g$ on $X$, depending only on $g_0,L,J_b$, such that $J_b$ is orthogonal and $J_bTL$ is perpendicular to $TL$ along $L$. For this metric there are constants $r_0,\varepsilon_0>0$ depending only on the geometric data and uniform family bounds with the following property. If $0<r\le r_0$ and a smooth map $u:\overline B_r^+\to X$ solves $u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$, maps the flat edge into $L$, and satisfies $E=\int_{B_r^+}e_g<\varepsilon_0$, then
$$|du(0,0)|_g^2\le\frac{32}{\pi r^2}E,\qquad \sup_{B_{r/2}^+}|du|_g^2\le\frac{128}{\pi r^2}E,$$
where $e_g=(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)/2$. Uniformly equivalent estimates with constants depending on the data hold for $g_0$. No assumption that the whole image lies in one coordinate chart is made.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact $(X,g)$, compact transverse totally real boundary submanifolds $L_0,L_1$ with finite intersection $K$, and smooth families $J_{n,t}$ converging smoothly to $J_{\infty,t}$. Their boundary structures on $L_0,L_1$ are fixed independently of $n$. Assume all these structures are exactly $i$ on common disjoint product generator charts taking $L_0,L_1$ to transverse product real lines, as in the actual transverse-strip neck lemma. Let smooth finite-energy solutions
$$\partial_su_n+J_{n,t}(u_n)\partial_tu_n=0,\qquad u_n(s,j)\in L_j,$$
on $\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ have energies at most $E_0$.

After a subsequence, either all maps are one constant generator, or there are finitely many longitudinal translations $q_{1,n}<\cdots<q_{M,n}$ with $q_{j+1,n}-q_{j,n}\to\infty$ and finitely many bubbled strip levels. Each level consists of a finite-energy $J_{\infty,t}$ strip, possibly constant, with finite sphere/disk bubble trees at its interior or physical boundary points. These are the actual local rescaling limits, have equal component values at their nodes, and constant bubbles satisfy the usual sphere node count or weighted disk node count. Each level has positive energy when its bubbles are included. The translated maps converge smoothly locally off the bubble points, including boundary derivatives, and all bubbles are smooth rescaled limits off their children.

After fixing the original end generators by a subsequence, adjacent strip levels have equal intermediate end generators, the first negative end and last positive end are the original ones, and
$$\lim_nE_g(u_n)=\sum_{j=1}^M\left(E_g(v_j)+\sum_{w\text{ on level }j}E_g(u_w)\right).$$
There is no energy or image diameter left between successive level cores or outside the first and last cores as their radii tend to infinity after the sequence limit. The number of levels and bubble components is uniformly bounded in terms of $E_0$ and the fixed geometric data. No exclusion of bubbles, index bound, regularity, or gluing is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$ for a closed connected Riemann surface, and fix finitely many product tori $L_j$ from systems of pairwise disjoint attaching curves. Let $a\in\Sigma$ lie off all these curves. The actual point-divisor bundle of $E_a=\{a\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}\Sigma$, with its canonical section on the boundary, defines integer degrees $n_a$ for disks and spheres, including contained spheres. It also defines an integer for every smooth strip between two transverse specified tori, with simultaneous product generator charts and uniform ends at their intersections: truncate and cap its ends inside sufficiently small generator charts avoiding $E_a$. The integer is independent of the sufficiently remote cuts and these local caps, and agrees with proper holomorphic intersection multiplicity whenever the latter is defined.

In the actual bounded-energy compactness conclusions of the bordered-source bubble-tree theorem, when the fixed source is a disk, or of the bubbled transverse-strip breaking theorem, these degrees satisfy, for all sufficiently large sequence indices,
$$n_a(u_n)=\sum_{\text{base or strip levels }v}n_a(v)+\sum_{\text{bubble components }w}n_a(w).$$
The hypotheses of those compactness theorems, including their common exact transverse generator charts for strips, are retained. No avoidance of $E_a$ by interior nodes or sphere bubbles is required. The formula holds simultaneously for any fixed finite set of such points.

In particular suppose the strip sequence satisfies that transverse-strip compactness theorem and the compact-bubble domain-energy lemma, with common diagonal and region-divisor neighborhoods and uniformly bounded geometric constants. Let $z_1,\ldots,z_k$ be marked points off all attaching curves, with $J_{n,t}$ and its limit equal to the standard symmetric-product structure near their divisors. Require that each connected component of the complement of each individual boundary curve system contains at least one of these marked points. If $n_{z_i}(u_n)=0$ for every $i,n$, its limit has no nonconstant sphere or disk bubbles. In fact no bubble vertices remain after discarding redundant constant vertices, and every retained strip level is nonconstant and has $n_{z_i}=0$ for every $i$. Thus that actual compactness theorem reduces to finite breaking of unbubbled zero-marked strips, with its smooth local convergence and full energy and neck-collapse conclusions. This does not assert regularity of same-generator index-two strips, a Maslov/domain-index identity, low-index stratum dimensions, or gluing.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $E$ be a smooth real rank-$2m$ vector bundle on $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, with a smooth endomorphism $J$ satisfying $J^2=-I$. On the two boundary edges let $F_0,F_1$ be smooth real rank-$m$ subbundles with $F_j\cap JF_j=0$. Suppose that outside a compact strip there are specified smooth complex frames $\tau_\pm:\mathbb C^m\to E$, intertwining $i$ and $J$, in which $F_0=\mathbb R^m$ and $F_1=i\mathbb R^m$. Let $P$ be a smooth real linear first-order operator on sections of $E$ with symbol
$$P(f\xi)=fP\xi+f_s\xi+f_tJ\xi$$
for every smooth real function $f$, and suppose its expression in each end frame is exactly $\partial_s+i\partial_t$ outside a compact strip.

There exist a global smooth complex frame $\Phi$, a sign matrix $S_+=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma,1,\ldots,1)$ with $\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$, an integer $\ell$, and a smooth real function $\vartheta(s)$, constant at $\pi/2$ on the negative end and $\pi/2+\ell\pi$ on the positive end, such that $\Phi=\tau_-$ on the negative end, $\Phi=\tau_+S_+$ on the positive end, and
$$F_0=\Phi\mathbb R^m,\qquad F_1=\Phi\left(e^{i\vartheta(s)}\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R^{m-1}\right).$$
In this frame $P$ is $\partial_s+i\partial_t+B(s,t)$ with smooth compactly supported real linear $B$. On the $H^1$ completion of compactly supported smooth sections satisfying those actual boundary subbundles, with the norm defined by finite bundle charts on a compact core and the prescribed frames on the ends, $P$ maps to the corresponding $L^2(E)$ space and is real Fredholm, with
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}P=-\ell.$$
The same index holds with the weight $e^{\delta|s|}$ for $0\le\delta<\pi/2$. These are indices before any translation quotient. The integer $\ell$ is independent of the choices in the construction, since it is minus the index of this fixed operator.

In particular the conclusion applies to the actual linearization at a smooth $J_t$-holomorphic strip of finite Dirichlet energy, measured in a smooth target metric, in a compact target, with compact totally real boundary submanifolds of transverse finite intersection, whenever the chosen target charts at their intersections identify those submanifolds with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t$ with the constant structure $i$ for every $t$. For product Heegaard tori such a geometric choice is available by the product-integrable generator-neighborhood construction. No domain Euler-measure formula, corner/excision theorem, generic regularity, or moduli count is part of this conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, and $0<\theta_j<\pi$. Write $X_0=H^1_\theta$ for the real $H^1$ completion of smooth maps compactly supported in $s$ satisfying $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$ and $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Let $B:S\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb C^m)$ be smooth up to the boundary, with every derivative bounded, and suppose its uniform end limits are real diagonal matrices $\operatorname{diag}(b_{\pm,j})$ with $\theta_j-b_{\pm,j}\notin\pi\mathbb Z$. For an integer $q\ge0$ put
$$X_q=H^{q+1}(S;\mathbb C^m)\cap X_0,\qquad Y_q=H^q(S;\mathbb C^m),\qquad T_q=\partial_s+i\partial_t+B:X_q\longrightarrow Y_q,$$
using real Hilbert spaces and their indicated Sobolev norms. There are no higher boundary conditions: only the zeroth trace encoded by $X_0$ is required. In particular no normal derivative or forcing trace is prescribed.

Every $T_q$ is bounded Fredholm. Its kernel is the same set as the kernel of $T_0$, and its range is $Y_q\cap\operatorname{Ran}T_0$. The inclusion of $Y_q$ in $L^2$ induces an isomorphism of real cokernels. Thus
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_q=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_0=\sum_j\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{-,j}}\pi\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{+,j}}\pi\right\rfloor\right).$$
More precisely, if $u\in X_0$ and $T_0u=f\in H^q$, then $u\in X_q$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{q+1}}\le C_q\bigl(\|f\|_{H^q}+\|u\|_{H^1}\bigr).$$

The same conclusions hold with smooth two-sided weights $w=e^{\delta\rho(s)}$, where $\rho$ is smooth, equals $|s|$ outside a compact interval, has all derivatives of positive order bounded, and $0\le\delta<\min_{\pm,j,n}|\pi n-\theta_j+b_{\pm,j}|$. Weighted spaces mean $wu\in X_q$ and $wf\in Y_q$. Their index is the same displayed index. The weight is smooth at zero even for $q\ge1$.

Finally, for an actual geometric strip operator with exact product-integrable ends and the smooth bundle frame supplied by the geometric strip normal-form theorem, the actual $H^{q+1}$ boundary-section domain and $H^q$ target have this same real index before translation quotient, also with these smooth weights. This asserts integer Hilbert Sobolev agreement; no $W^{1,p}$ comparison or Heegaard-domain Euler formula is asserted.

Assume countable choice. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold with a smooth path $J_t$ of almost complex structures, and let $L_0,L_1$ be compact submanifolds totally real for $J_0,J_1$, respectively. Suppose their intersection is finite and transverse. At each intersection point choose a target chart in which $L_0=\mathbb R^m$, $L_1=i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t=i$ for every $t$. Retain those same charts and structures throughout.

A smooth fixed-end representative from $x$ to $y$ is a smooth map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ with boundary on $L_0,L_1$, identically $x$ on one full negative tail and identically $y$ on one full positive tail. Its covariant Cauchy–Riemann linearization on fixed-end $H^1\to L^2$ spaces is Fredholm. Its real index is independent of the chosen smooth connection and of the representative under any smooth relative homotopy $H(h,s,t)$ with those boundary conditions, fixed endpoints, and one common pair of constant tails for all $h\in[0,1]$.

These indices add under concatenating two such representatives at their common endpoint, are zero for a constant representative, and change sign when $u(s,t)$ is replaced by $u(-s,t)$. Thus they define an integer index on smooth fixed-end representatives modulo the stated smooth relative homotopies, with concatenation and reversal laws. This result includes nonholomorphic representatives. It does not assume that a nonlinear moduli space exists or is regular.

A further relative smoothing and end-flattening argument is required to identify this smooth quotient with a Whitney-class set defined initially by arbitrary continuous disk maps and continuous relative homotopies. No such identification, domain Euler formula, or arbitrary-class representativity theorem is asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $u$ be an actual smooth finite-energy strip in the compact exact-generator geometry of the actual higher Sobolev strip-chart construction, and let $P:H^1\cap\mathcal X^1\to L^2$ be its geometric Cauchy–Riemann linearization. Use any fixed smooth positive definite target metric and source measure $ds\,dt$ to define the real $L^2$ pairing. Every $\eta\in L^2$ which annihilates $\operatorname{Ran}P$ has a smooth representative on $\mathbb R\times(0,1)$. In each smooth local frame that representative satisfies the actual formal adjoint equation. For compact subsets $K\subset\operatorname{int}U$ in a coordinate patch inside the strip and every integer $q\ge0$,
$$\|\eta\|_{H^q(K)}\le C_{K,U,q}\|\eta\|_{L^2(U)},$$
where the constant depends on the indicated compact containment and finitely many local smooth coefficient and metric bounds. No boundary regularity or adjoint boundary formula is asserted.

More generally, let $K_0:H\to H^2(u^*TX)$ be any bounded linear parameter derivative from a real Hilbert space, including the actual derivative $b\mapsto(d_aJ[b])_t(u)u_t$ of the smooth Hilbert family. The operators
$$A_0(\xi,b)=P\xi+K_0b:\ (H^1\cap\mathcal X^1)\oplus H\longrightarrow L^2,$$
$$A_2(\xi,b)=P\xi+K_0b:\ (H^3\cap\mathcal X^1)\oplus H\longrightarrow H^2$$
both have closed range, and $A_0$ is onto if and only if $A_2$ is onto. They are onto exactly when there is no nonzero $L^2$ section $\eta$ such that
$$\langle\eta,P\xi\rangle_{L^2}=0\quad\hbox{for every }\xi\in H^1\cap\mathcal X^1,\qquad \langle\eta,K_0b\rangle_{L^2}=0\quad\hbox{for every }b\in H.$$
Each such obstruction is smooth on the interior by the first assertion. Thus actual interior unique continuation can be applied to an $L^2$ obstruction after this lemma; an $H^2$-dual distribution need not be mistaken for an $L^2$ function. The lemma does not prove unique continuation or rule out the displayed obstructions.

Assume countable choice and write $D=\partial_s+i\partial_t=2\partial_{\bar z}$ on a connected open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$. Let $B\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb C^m))$, and let $v\in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb C^m)$, for some $p>2$, solve $Dv+Bv=0$ weakly. Use its continuous representative. Near every point $z_0$ there are a continuous invertible complex matrix $P$, belonging locally to $W^{1,q}$ for every finite $q>2$, and a holomorphic vector function $h$ with $v=Ph$. One may normalize $P(z_0)=I$.

Consequently either $v$ is identically zero, or all its zeros are isolated and have finite order: at a zero $z_0$ there are an integer $k\ge1$ and constants $c,C,r>0$ with
$$c|z-z_0|^k\le|v(z)|\le C|z-z_0|^k\qquad(0<|z-z_0|<r).$$
In particular vanishing on an open set, or vanishing to infinite order at one point, forces global vanishing. The same conclusions hold for $v_s+J(s,t)v_t+Av=0$ when $J$ is a smooth family of real complex structures and $A$ is locally bounded; the local factor is then an invertible real matrix rather than necessarily a complex matrix.

If two smooth maps solve the same equation $u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$ for a smooth almost complex family on a smooth target and have matching infinite jets at one interior point, they agree everywhere on their connected common source. Agreement on an open set suffices. This assertion concerns parametrized maps and actual linear equations; it does not infer moduli transversality or an injective-point theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact $(X,g)$, compact transverse boundary submanifolds $L_0,L_1$, and a smooth $J_t$ with fixed totally real boundary structures. Suppose fixed disjoint generator charts about their finite intersection identify the boundaries with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t$ with $i$ for every $t$. Fix end generators $x_-,x_+$ and $0\le\delta<\pi/2$, using a smooth weight $e^{\delta\rho(s)}$ as in the weighted Sobolev algebra lemma.

There is an actual second-countable separable real Hilbert configuration manifold $\mathcal B_\delta$ of strip maps with these boundary values and ends, constructed as the union of the following local charts. A reference map $u_0$ is smooth, satisfies the boundary condition, and equals $x_\pm$ outside a compact longitudinal interval. Its tangent model is
$$\mathcal X_{u_0}=H^3_\delta(u_0^*TX)\cap\mathcal X^1_{u_0},$$
where $\mathcal X^1_{u_0}$ is the $H^1$ completion of compactly supported smooth tangent sections satisfying $TL_0,TL_1$ on the edges. This is an intersection with the $H^1$ domain, not an asserted $H^3$ closure. Small sections give maps $u=\mathcal E(u_0,\xi)$ for the actual boundary-preserving local addition. All smooth finite-energy $J_t$ strips with these ends belong to this manifold.

The actual Cauchy–Riemann expression $u_s+J_t(u)u_t$ defines a smooth section of the Hilbert bundle with fiber $H^2_\delta(u^*TX)$. In the local-addition trivialization it is a smooth map $\mathcal F_{u_0}:\mathcal X_{u_0}\to H^2_\delta(u_0^*TX)$. On a small norm ball its nonlinear remainder obeys
$$\|\mathcal F(\xi)-\mathcal F(\eta)-D\mathcal F(0)(\xi-\eta)\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C(\|\xi\|_{H^3_\delta}+\|\eta\|_{H^3_\delta})\|\xi-\eta\|_{H^3_\delta}.$$
The constants are uniform for reference families with uniform coefficient/frame derivatives through the orders used in this estimate. Every zero is smooth and has finite energy and the prescribed ends. At each zero the derivative is the actual geometric Fredholm linearization $H^3_\delta\cap\mathcal X^1\to H^2_\delta$, with the same real index as its $H^1\to L^2$ realization, before translation quotient. No universal transversality or gluing is claimed.

Assume Countable Choice and put $S=\mathbb R\times(0,1)$. For $k=1,2,3$ there is a bounded linear extension $H^k(S)\to H^k(\mathbb R^2)$, using no boundary condition. The spaces have the estimates $H^1(S)\subset L^4(S)$, $H^2(S)\subset C^0(\overline S)\cap L^\infty(S)$, and $H^3(S)\subset C^1(\overline S)$, with bounded supremum norms in the last two assertions. In particular
$$\|fg\|_{H^2}\le C\|f\|_{H^2}\|g\|_{H^2}.$$

Fix smooth $\rho\ge0$ equal to $|s|$ outside a compact interval, with bounded derivatives, and $\delta\ge0$. Set $w=e^{\delta\rho}$ and $\|u\|_{H^k_\delta}=\|wu\|_{H^k}$. The same embeddings hold with $w|u|$, or $w(|u|+|du|)$ for $k=3$, bounded by the weighted norm. Products satisfy
$$\|fg\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C_\delta\|f\|_{H^2_\delta}\|g\|_{H^2_\delta},\qquad \|du\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C_\delta\|u\|_{H^3_\delta}.$$

Let $h(s,t,z)$ be smooth up to the boundary for $z$ in a finite-dimensional ball about zero, with bounded mixed derivatives of source order at most two and every finite target order on smaller target balls, and $h(s,t,0)=0$. Then $u\mapsto h(s,t,u)$ is a smooth map from the open subset of $H^2_\delta$ whose supremum lies in that ball to $H^2_\delta$. Its derivatives are the ordinary pointwise derivatives of $h$. On a sufficiently small bounded norm ball the remainder $Q(u)=h(s,t,u)-h_z(s,t,0)u$ satisfies
$$\|Q(u)-Q(v)\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C\bigl(\|u\|_{H^2_\delta}+\|v\|_{H^2_\delta}\bigr)\|u-v\|_{H^2_\delta}.$$
All statements hold componentwise for finite-dimensional real or complex targets.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $M,N$ be Hausdorff second-countable $C^r$ manifolds modeled on separable real Hilbert spaces, and let $f:M\to N$ be $C^r$, where $r$ is a positive integer or $\infty$. Suppose every derivative $Df(x)$ is a bounded Fredholm operator of the same index $d$ and $r>\max\{d,0\}$. Then the regular values of $f$ form a dense residual subset of $N$. A value is regular if every derivative at its inverse images is surjective; values with empty inverse image are regular.

Here Hilbert completeness means convergence of Cauchy sequences. No arbitrary-index choice or dependent-choice axiom is assumed. This theorem concerns a map already known to be Fredholm; it does not establish Fredholmness of a differential operator or transversality of its universal solution space.

Assume countable choice. Let $E,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $f$ a $C^1$ map on an open neighborhood of the closed ball $\overline B_E(0,r)$, and $D=df(0)$. Suppose a specified bounded linear map $Q:Y\to E$ satisfies $DQ=I_Y$. Fix $M>0$, $L\ge0$ with $\|Q\|\le M$ and
$$\|df(x)-df(y)\|\le L\|x-y\|\quad(x,y\in\overline B_E(0,r)).$$
Put $\varepsilon=\|f(0)\|$. If
$$2M\varepsilon<r,\qquad MLr\le\tfrac12,$$
then there is a unique $x\in\operatorname{im}Q\cap\overline B_E(0,r)$ with $f(x)=0$. It satisfies
$$\|x\|\le2M\varepsilon,\qquad \|x+Qf(0)\|\le2M^3L\varepsilon^2.$$
The sequence $x_0=0$,
$$x_{n+1}=-Qf(0)-Q\bigl(f(x_n)-f(0)-Dx_n\bigr)$$
converges to this correction, with contraction ratio at most $1/2$. At the corrected zero $df(x)$ is still surjective, with specified right inverse
$$Q_x=Q\bigl[I_Y+(df(x)-D)Q\bigr]^{-1},\qquad \|Q_x\|\le2M.$$

The following local smooth conclusions also hold. If $f(0)=0$, $f$ is $C^q$, $1\le q\le\infty$, and $D$ has the specified bounded right inverse $Q$, continuity of $df$ alone suffices for a local $C^q$ zero-set chart. With $K=\ker D$ and $V=\operatorname{im}Q$, there is a $C^q$ map $v$ from a neighborhood of $0$ in $K$ to $V$, with $v(0)=dv(0)=0$, such that, in a product neighborhood for $E=K\oplus V$,
$$f(k+w)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w=v(k).$$
For a $C^q$ family $f(p,z)$, $p$ in any Banach parameter space, the same assertion holds locally with $v=v(p,k)$ whenever $f(p_0,0)=0$ and $d_zf(p_0,0)Q=I_Y$. In particular, if $Q(p)$ is a specified $C^q$ family of right inverses to $d_zf(p,0)$ and the quantitative hypotheses hold strictly with locally uniform constants, the unique corrections in $\operatorname{im}Q(p)$ depend $C^q$ on $p$.

This is an abstract correction and chart theorem. It assumes the right inverse and all displayed estimates; it supplies no geometric pregluing, uniform right-inverse construction, Fredholm index, or gluing exhaustion theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix a globally weakly admissible complete pointed Heegaard diagram of any closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold and a fixed positive surface area form. Supply a smooth finite-parameter family of surface complex structures and the actual relative symmetric-product transports and compatible families with one canonical full boundary structure on BOTH tori and common exact generator charts. There exist genuine canonical endpoint time-collar paths regular at every zero-basepoint strip, with these common boundary neighborhoods and the prescribed protected backgrounds. Their actual finite index-one counts define chosen hat complexes. Let $C^0,C^1$ be any such regular chosen endpoint complexes in this supplied common-boundary family.

There exist genuine compact-transition continuation data, permitting the actual $t$-independent ordered-lifted connection forcing of the positive-domain/energy lemma, for which all zero-basepoint solutions are regular. Their actual index-zero solutions, counted WITHOUT a translation quotient, form a finite matrix $\Phi:C^0\to C^1$. This is a chain map and a chain-homotopy equivalence. Within the supplied finite-parameter family its chain-homotopy class is independent of the source profile, adapted connection and regular perturbations relative the two fixed endpoint paths. Composition is represented by actual concatenated data up to an actual finite index-minus-one continuation homotopy. The identities and inverse homotopies are obtained from actual compact one-manifolds with their exhaustive gluing collars.

Genus zero gives the identity of the one-generator complex. The comparison covers the chosen canonical-boundary endpoint complexes on this fixed globally weak diagram, while genuinely changing the surface complex structure. It does not compare arbitrary preassigned full boundary structures, sector-only admissibility, area changes without the stated common energy interface, Heegaard attaching-circle moves, integral orientations, absolute gradings or plus/infinity/cobordism packages. No assertion about a symmetric power of a nonholomorphic surface map is made.

Assume Countable Choice and the common fixed-background globally weak closed-diagram geometry of [[thm-fixed-background-hat-data-admit-regular-finite-continuation-counts]]. The following two actual gluing assertions hold, with zero basepoint degree throughout.

First let $q\in\{0,1\}$, let $a$ vary near an interior point $a_0\in\mathbb R^q$, and let $K_a(s,t)$ be a smooth family equal to fixed autonomous paths $J^\pm_t$ outside one common compact longitudinal interval. The time collars, protected values and exact generator charts are common. Let $u$ be an actual central solution at $a_0$, with index $-q$, such that its ACTUAL augmented derivative
$$\mathbb R^q\oplus H^3_u\longrightarrow H^2_u,\qquad(\dot a,\xi)\longmapsto P_u\xi+(\partial_aK_a[\dot a])(s,t,u)u_t$$
is onto. Thus it is an isomorphism, its index being zero. Let $v$ be an actual regular autonomous index-one strip on either end, with matching generator. Then that ordered central/end pair has an actual injective exhaustive half-interval gluing collar in the augmented family of total index $1-q$, with no longitudinal translation quotient of the central solution. Its interior consists of actual solutions regular in the stipulated AUGMENTED family, and every bounded-energy sequence converging to precisely that pair with no other components is eventually in this collar. The central family parameter is solved as part of gluing. For $q=0$ the collar lies in the fixed continuation moduli of index one; for $q=1$ it lies in the parameterized continuation moduli of index zero. Class and basepoint degree are the actual concatenated ones.

Second let $K^{01},K^{12}$ be two compact-transition choices whose EVERY zero-basepoint solution is regular, with common autonomous middle end $J^1$ and outer ends $J^0,J^2$, all of whose nonconstant zero-basepoint autonomous strips are regular. Translate their transition supports to centers $-R/2,+R/2$, and join them by their identical middle value $J^1$, obtaining a genuine smooth structure $K^R$ for every sufficiently large $R$. For all sufficiently large $R$, every zero-basepoint solution for $K^R$ is regular, its actual index-zero solution set is finite, and that set is in bijection with pairs of actual index-zero solutions for $K^{01},K^{12}$ having a common intermediate generator. The bijection is actual gluing, with no extra multiplicity and with each pair's continuous concatenated class. Consequently their finite mod-two index-zero matrices satisfy
$$\Phi_{K^R}=\Phi_{K^{12}}\Phi_{K^{01}}.$$
This assertion includes constant component solutions. It does not assert that the family of maps as $R$ varies is injective when both components are constant.

These are gluing/collar and finite composition-count statements. Chain-map and homotopy identities require the corresponding actual one-manifold compactifications; no polygon or Heegaard move map is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice and the complete marked nearly symmetric geometry, protected neighborhoods and exact product generator charts of the zero-marked bubble-exclusion lemma. Fix $E_0<\infty$, end generators $x_-,x_+$, and an actual smooth path $J_t$ for which every nonconstant zero-marked strip of energy at most $E_0$ has surjective actual linearization. Such a path with genuine endpoint collars is supplied by the bounded-energy collar-openness lemma.

There are finitely many longitudinal-translation orbits of nonconstant zero-marked $J_t$ strips from $x_-$ to $x_+$ with energy at most $E_0$ and real Fredholm index one. This remains true simultaneously over the finite set of ordered end pairs. Their counts modulo two are therefore well-defined integers modulo two. The index is the actual $H^1\to L^2$ operator index, before translation quotient. No identification with a separately named Maslov or domain index is asserted, and the theorem supplies no energy bound for an unrestricted collection of Floer classes.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix the compact nearly symmetric Heegaard geometry with complete marked cut systems, protected diagonal and region-divisor neighborhoods, and common exact product generator charts used in zero-marked bubble exclusion. Every complement component of each individual boundary curve system must contain a marked point. Whitney classes mean continuous two-marked disk relative-homotopy classes with the two boundary arcs on the specified product tori. Their integer $\mu$ is the actual fixed-end Fredholm index constructed by continuous relative smoothing, not a domain Euler formula.

Fix a class $\phi:x\to z$ with $\mu(\phi)=2$ and with all marked divisor degrees zero. Its region divisor degrees $n_R(\phi)$ are well-defined integers. For a common domain-energy constant $C$ put
$$B_\phi=C\sum_R|n_R(\phi)|\int_R\eta.$$
Choose a smooth path with genuine constant endpoint collars, the stipulated protected data, and actual regularity for every nonconstant zero-marked strip of energy at most a number $E_0>B_\phi$. Such paths exist by the auxiliary flat-jet regularity and actual bounded-energy collar-approximation theorems, with $C$ taken uniform in the approximating neighborhood as proved below.

For this path, the moduli space $\widehat{\mathcal M}(\phi)$ of actual strips in $\phi$ modulo longitudinal translation is a Hausdorff second-countable topological one-manifold. It has a compactification by finitely many boundary points. These points are exactly the ordered pairs of actual index-one strip orbits
$$([u],[v]),\qquad u:x\to y,\quad v:y\to z,\quad [u]*[v]=\phi.$$
Each such component has zero marked degrees and energy at most $B_\phi$. Each boundary point has the actual one-sided gluing collar with smooth interior from the regular-pair collar theorem. No differentiability at a prescribed compactifying parameter is asserted.

The number of these boundary points is even. Equivalently the sum modulo two of the products of rigid counts over the factorizations $\phi=\phi_1*\phi_2$ with $\mu(\phi_1)=\mu(\phi_2)=1$ is zero; only finitely many factors with nonzero counts occur. This is the cancellation identity for this fixed zero-marked class. It does not establish finiteness over all classes of prescribed index, a domain-index formula, positive-marked boundary-degeneration cancellation, or polygon/target-degeneration gluing.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The point target in genus zero gives the assertion directly. Otherwise choose a smooth homogeneous physical interpolation $J(s,t)$, equal to the prescribed end paths outside a fixed source interval. Use the fixed compatible reference and its tame Cayley coefficients on the complement of the protected diagonal, and interpolate those coefficients. Their operator norms are strictly less than one, so the convex combination is tame. Both endpoints agree on the protected neighborhoods and generator charts; these values are unchanged. On a common smaller physical-time collar each endpoint is independent of t, hence so is the interpolation. No equality of its two endpoint torus values across s is imposed. The same construction gives finite-parameter physical profile homotopies relative the actual source ends. Apply [F1] to these varying torus boundary values, with one reference $J_b$, to get actual t-independent target diffeomorphisms $P_s$ fixing BOTH tori pointwise, identity on smaller generator charts and near all protected divisors and the diagonal. They are stationary at the source ends. With physical $u=P_sv$ the exact normalized equation is $$v_s+K(s,t,v)v_t=W(s,v),\qquad K=P_s^*J,\quad W=-(dP_s)^{-1}\partial_sP_s.$$ Its full boundary value is the fixed $J_b$ and W vanishes ON both tori, not necessarily near them. The same is true in every finite-parameter homotopy. [F1, A1, given, construct]

Obtain the uniform energy in PHYSICAL coordinates. Fixed j near the divisors gives nonnegative local multiplicities for every physical source-dependent solution. The finite collision set and finite ordered branched-cover proof of [F2] applies literally: its local collision equation is the same integrable equation, and off that set the pulled-up CR structure is pointwise tame for the fixed product area. Thus the ordered physical lift has energy at most its oriented area times one constant. The signed degree integral is the cover degree times $\sum_Rn_R\operatorname{Area}_\eta(R)$. Source derivatives of J do not enter this calculation. Global weakness makes the normalized nonnegative domain sets finite over ALL endpoint pairs before any index restriction: an unbounded affine integral slice would normalize to a nonzero nonnegative real periodic vector; rational-face approximation and clearing denominators contradict admissibility. There is consequently one physical energy bound B over all these profiles. The actual finite-domain homotopies preserve domains under $P_s$, since these maps fix both tori pointwise, preserve the chosen divisors and generator caps and are isotopic to identity with all those properties. Uniform derivatives of $P_s^{\pm1}$ give $$E(v)\le C E(u)+C\int_{\mathbb R}\|\partial_sP_s\|_\infty^2ds.$$ This is uniformly finite on the compact profile families. The normalized K is tame for $P_s^*\omega$; no false fixed-form tameness is used. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

Verify boundary analysis for ON-torus vanishing. Use on source patch times X the graph structure $\mathcal J\partial_t=-\partial_s-W$, $\mathcal J\partial_s=\partial_t+KW$, $\mathcal J\xi=K\xi$. Its square is -I and its holomorphic graphs are exactly the normalized solutions. On $\mathbb R\times L_e$ the full tensor is independent of s: W is ZERO at every point of $L_e$, and K there is the full fixed $J_b$. Hence this graph boundary is totally real and satisfies precisely the fixed-boundary hypothesis of [F3]'s boundary epsilon theorem. Normal derivatives of W need not vanish; they enter only the uniformly bounded derivatives of this smooth graph tensor. Compactify the local base coordinate patch by smooth coordinate cutoffs as in [F5]; graph energy is $E(v)+O(r^2)$ on a radius-r disk. The actual interior/boundary epsilon estimates, smooth bootstrap, finite rescaling and energy-atom induction therefore apply with uniform constants. Rescaling sends the smooth bounded W to zero. In the frozen physical target each bubble has the actual nearly symmetric frozen J, not an equation with an unexamined residual force. [F1, F3, F5, step 2.1, construct]

The genuine bad-window extraction gives one unshifted central solution and finitely many ordered nonconstant autonomous end levels. Outside the compact force interval use the homogeneous epsilon estimate directly, so no graph base-area term obstructs long-window selection. On low-energy gaps, derivative decay and transverse slice compactness put the entire slice in one generator chart. There the actual equation is exactly $D_0$ because P is identity and W=0 on that NEIGHBORHOOD. The actual Fourier neck estimate proves energy AND image collapse; on shrinking bubble annuli the smooth bounded force contributes only a vanishing area term. This proves full energy-complete anchored compactness, using [F3]'s actual extraction rather than invoking its autonomous Statement for a forced equation. The fixed $E_z$ line connection flat near both tori and generator charts has degree $-(2\pi i)^{-1}\int v^*F$. Smooth core convergence and missing energy bound all omitted curvature integrals by $C E_{\mathrm{omitted}}$, so degrees add across all components. P preserves this divisor and its orientation. Every frozen nonconstant sphere or one-torus disk has positive z-degree by [F3]'s complete-cut compact-bubble theorem, while all strip degrees are nonnegative by step2.1. Total z-degree zero excludes all nonconstant bubbles; a finite stable tree consisting only of ghosts has an unstable terminal vertex. The limit is genuinely unbubbled finite breaking. [F1, F2, F3, step 3.1, construct]

Scalar real cutoffs on the exact generator necks preserve both boundary planes and give actual relative homotopies splitting the eventual Whitney class into its central and end classes. Local addition identifies the converging finite cores. To identify operator indices BEFORE regularity, vary the PHYSICAL tame coefficients to one fixed compatible reference using their convex Cayley path, retaining protected/gen values, and apply the explicit boundary-jet normalization to that whole homotopy. All normalized boundary values remain $J_b$, all whole generator tails remain $D_0$, and W is a smooth compact-source zeroth-order term. The actual finite-core framed parametrix and higher weak range proof in [F4] therefore keep these operators Fredholm throughout, independently of a fixed global normalized taming form. Constant generator caps cancel under concatenation, giving the index of the sequence equal to the central index plus the sum of end indices. This argument does not assume component regularity to prove additivity. Regular nonconstant autonomous levels have index at least one from translation; a regular central level has index at least zero without a translation quotient. [F1, F4, step 4.1, construct]

Construct genuine universal regularity. Keep the PHYSICAL boundary values $J(s,e)|_{L_e}$ of the chosen base profile fixed during its perturbations, so the already constructed $P_s$ and W stay fixed. Enumerate rational smooth anti-J matrix bumps in source AND target, supported off the protected diagonal/divisors, fixed generator neighborhoods and BOTH tori. Rapid $\ell^2$ weights, with all source derivatives and all exponential source norms through order n in the nth denominator, give a smooth family in every finite coefficient norm, flat in physical-time jets and rapidly asymptotic to the specified ends. Its Cayley derivative spans every allowed tangent fiber densely. Pullback by P preserves this density at each free site. The actual $H^3\cap H^1_{\mathrm{boundary}}\to H^2$ section is smooth by [F4]'s algebra; W adds a bounded smooth Nemytskij term, with derivative -dW. Hence $v_t$ cannot vanish on an open set for a nonconstant solution. If it did, UC would make v t-independent, so its values lie in the finite transverse intersection and it is one generator. Prove a free point without assuming neighborhood vanishing. Suppose a nonconstant map had image in $D\cup L_0\cup L_1\cup G$. Connectedness and its boundary values keep that image in the component containing $L_0\cup L_1\cup G$, away from the separated D. An anti-K target endomorphism Y can send $v_t$ to that obstruction. A nonnegative source-and-target bump gives a strictly positive integrated pairing; source localization isolates the relevant source rectangle without any injective-target assumption. The actual split zero charts and CC Hilbert Sard now choose an auxiliary profile regular at EVERY zero-basepoint solution, countably over all index strata and the finite endpoint pairs. Replace its flat-jet/source-decaying coefficient by genuine time-collar and compact-source cutoffs; all derivatives converge uniformly, including in the parameterized relative version. Perturbations vanish along both tori, so their truncations preserve the chosen boundary values and the SAME $P_s,W$. The energy bound and anchored compactness were proved before genericity. If a sequence of truncations had cokernels, its limit is one auxiliary regular central solution and finitely many regular given autonomous end levels, with no bubbles. On fixed cores identify the actual bundles by local addition. Patch their specified bounded right inverses with squared cutoffs $\sum_j\eta_j^2=1$ changing over long exact $D_0$ necks. The first-order Leibniz identity gives right-inverse error at most $C(\delta_n+R^{-1})$: fixed-core coefficient errors are $\delta_n\to0$, and commutators are $O(R^{-1})$. The -dW term stays on the fixed central core. First fix large R, then large n, and Neumann-correct the inverse; this contradicts a cokernel. All sufficiently late truncations are genuinely regular. For a relative parameter family use bumps flat at its fixed parameter endpoints, Sard on its open interior, and the onto fixed-profile operators at the endpoints. The SAME inverse patch retains the one finite parameter output only on the central core; parameter derivatives vanish on generator necks and autonomous ends. This yields an actual augmented-regular genuine family, neat at its prescribed regular endpoints. [F1, F3, F4, step 4.1, step 7.1, construct]

For index-zero central solutions, step5.1 and regularity of ALL limiting components prohibit any nonconstant end level. Thus anchored compactness gives an unbroken regular index-zero limit. The exact tail inverse upgrades local smooth convergence to global $H^3$: for a fixed far-tail cutoff, the difference satisfies $D_0(\chi w)=\chi' w$, so the bounded inverse and higher range estimates control its whole tail by a fixed convergent transition band. Its actual zero chart has dimension zero and isolates the limit.
